author: audit_053
noChangeCaveat: Only indicates this draft proposes no edit after initial comparison; not independent approval or guarantee of no defect.

rows.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。

before.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.
before.idiomatic: Sima Yu, styled Xizu, was Emperor Hui's firstborn—his mother was Lady Xie of Talented rank.

after.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.
after.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai, Sima Yu, styled Xizu, was Emperor Hui’s eldest son. His mother was Lady Xie, a Talented Lady.

rows.note: Restore the posthumous title used in the source; 才人 is a palace rank.

rows.zh: 嘗與諸皇子共戲殿上，惠帝來朝，執諸皇子手，次至太子，帝曰：「是汝兒也。」

before.literal: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'
before.idiomatic: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience, he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, the emperor said, 'This is your son.'

after.literal: Once he was playing in the hall with the imperial princes when Emperor Hui came to court and took each prince by the hand. When he came to the crown prince, the emperor said, “This is your son.”
after.idiomatic: Once, as he played in the hall with the imperial princes, Emperor Hui came to court and took each prince by the hand. When he reached the crown prince, the emperor said, “This is your son.”

rows.note: 殿上 is in/on the hall, not necessarily on its steps; the speaker is Wu in context. Retain the independently reviewed identification of who takes hands.

rows.zh: 宮中嘗夜失火，武帝登樓望之。

before.literal: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.
before.idiomatic: A night blaze drew Wu Di to a high gallery.

after.literal: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.
after.idiomatic: Once, when a fire broke out in the palace at night, Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.

rows.note: Restore the palace, the emperor, and that he climbed to look.

rows.zh: 帝問其故，太子曰：「暮夜倉卒，宜備非常，不宜令照見人君也。」

before.literal: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'
before.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "Suddenly at night one must guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face."

after.literal: The emperor asked the reason, and the crown prince said, “In a sudden emergency at night, one should guard against the unexpected; the ruler should not be exposed to the light.”
after.idiomatic: The emperor asked why, and the crown prince replied, “At night, when an emergency arises, one should be on guard against the unexpected. The ruler should not be exposed to the light.”

rows.note: Restore the emperor’s question omitted in the idiomatic field; 照見 does not explicitly specify the ruler’s face.

rows.zh: 嘗從帝觀豕牢，言於帝曰：「豕甚肥，何不殺以享士，而使久費五穀？」

before.literal: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, 'The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?'
before.idiomatic: While watching the imperial sty he said to the emperor, "The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?"

after.literal: Once, when he accompanied the emperor to look at the pigpen, he said, “The pigs are very fat. Why not slaughter them to feast the men, instead of letting them go on consuming grain?”
after.idiomatic: Once, while accompanying the emperor to the pigpen, he asked, “The pigs are so fat—why not slaughter them to feast the men rather than letting them go on consuming grain?”

rows.note: 久 does not mean forever; retain accompanying the emperor and the proposed feast.

rows.zh: 帝嘉其意，即使烹之。

before.literal: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.
before.idiomatic: Wu Di approved and had them slaughtered.

after.literal: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.
after.idiomatic: Emperor Wu approved of the suggestion and immediately ordered the pigs cooked.

rows.note: 烹 is to cook, not just slaughter; 即 is immediate.

rows.zh: 嘗對群臣稱太子似宣帝，於是令譽流於天下。

before.literal: He once declared before the assembled ministers that the crown prince resembled Emperor Xuan; thereafter praise of him spread through the realm.
before.idiomatic: He likened the heir to Sima Yi before court—reputation followed.

after.literal: He once declared before the assembled ministers that the crown prince resembled Emperor Xuan; thereafter praise of him spread through the realm.
after.idiomatic: He once told the assembled ministers that the crown prince resembled Emperor Xuan, and praise of the prince spread throughout the realm.

rows.note: Restore once, assembled ministers, formal appellation, and spread throughout the realm.

rows.zh: 及長，不好學，惟與左右嬉戲，不能尊敬保傅。

before.literal: When grown he cared nothing for study and only played games with attendants; he could not honor tutors or guardians.
before.idiomatic: Adult Yu spurned books, slighted tutors, and played with pages.

after.literal: When he grew older, he disliked study and only played with his attendants; he failed to respect his guardians and tutors.
after.idiomatic: As he grew older, he neglected his studies, played with his attendants, and showed no respect for his guardians and tutors.

rows.note: 及長 means grew older, not necessarily an adult; 左右 need not be pages.

rows.zh: 賈后素忌太子有令譽，因此密敕黃門閹宦媚諛于太子曰：「殿下誠可及壯時極意所欲，何為恆自拘束？」

before.literal: Empress Jia had long envied the crown prince's fine reputation and therefore secretly ordered Yellow Gate eunuchs to flatter him: 'Your Highness may indeed indulge every whim while still young—why bind yourself so tightly?'
before.idiomatic: Empress Jia secretly ordered Yellow Gate eunuchs to flatter the crown prince: "Your Highness may indeed indulge every whim while still young—why bind yourself so tightly?"

after.literal: Empress Jia had long envied the crown prince's fine reputation and therefore secretly ordered Yellow Gate eunuchs to flatter him: 'Your Highness may indeed indulge every whim while still young—why bind yourself so tightly?'
after.idiomatic: Empress Jia had long resented the crown prince’s good reputation, so she secretly instructed the Yellow Gate eunuchs to flatter him: “Your Highness should indulge your desires while you are young. Why always restrain yourself?”

rows.note: Restore the reason omitted from the idiomatic.

rows.zh: 每見喜怒之際，輒歎曰：「殿下不知用威刑，天下豈得畏服！」

before.literal: Whenever she saw him angry or pleased she would sigh, 'Your Highness does not know how to wield awe and punishment—how will the realm ever fear and obey!'
before.idiomatic: Whenever she saw him angry or pleased she would sigh, "Your Highness does not know how to wield awe and punishment—how will the realm ever fear and obey!"

after.literal: Whenever they saw signs of his pleasure or anger, they would sigh, “Your Highness does not know how to use authority and punishment. How can the realm fear and obey you?”
after.idiomatic: Whenever they saw him pleased or angry, the eunuchs would sigh, “Your Highness does not know how to use authority and punishment. How can anyone under Heaven fear and obey you?”

rows.note: The plural eunuchs are the speakers in the preceding sentence, not necessarily the empress; reviewer must confirm.

rows.zh: 太子所幸蔣美人生男，又言宜隆其賞賜，多為皇孫造玩弄之器，太子從之。

before.literal: When Lady Jiang, whom the crown prince favored, bore a son, they also said rewards should be lavish and many toys fashioned for the imperial grandson; the crown prince obeyed.
before.idiomatic: When Consort Jiang bore a son they pushed costly toys and stipends—Yu complied.

after.literal: When Lady Jiang, whom the crown prince favored, bore a son, they also said rewards should be lavish and many toys fashioned for the imperial grandson; the crown prince obeyed.
after.idiomatic: When the crown prince’s favored Lady Jiang bore a son, they also urged him to give lavish rewards and make many toys for the imperial grandson. The crown prince followed their advice.

rows.note: Restore rewards, objects made for the grandson, and their advice; stipends are not specified.

rows.zh: 於是慢弛益彰，或廢朝侍，恆在後園遊戲。

before.literal: Thereupon his arrogance and laxness grew plainer; sometimes he skipped court attendance and constantly played in the rear garden.
before.idiomatic: He skipped audiences for back-garden games.

after.literal: Thereupon his arrogance and laxness grew plainer; sometimes he skipped court attendance and constantly played in the rear garden.
after.idiomatic: His arrogance and laxity became increasingly evident; he sometimes neglected court attendance and spent his time playing in the rear garden.

rows.note: Restore increasing arrogance and frequency; 或 does not say every audience was skipped.

rows.zh: 愛埤車小馬，令左右馳騎，斷其鞅勒，使墮地為樂。

before.literal: He loved low carts and ponies, ordering attendants to gallop them, cutting cheek-straps and cheek-pieces so riders fell for sport.
before.idiomatic: He staged pony-cart wrecks for amusement.

after.literal: He loved little carts and ponies and had his attendants ride at speed. He cut their harness straps and reins so that they would fall to the ground, which he found amusing.
after.idiomatic: He delighted in little carts and ponies, making his attendants ride fast and cutting their harness straps and reins so they fell to the ground, to his amusement.

rows.note: Review exactly which harness pieces 鞅勒 indicates; avoid inventing cart wrecks.

rows.zh: 或有犯忤者，手自捶擊之。

before.literal: If anyone offended him he personally beat them.
before.idiomatic: He thrashed servants himself.

after.literal: If anyone offended him he personally beat them.
after.idiomatic: If someone offended him, he beat that person with his own hands.

rows.note: Do not restrict the victim to servants.

rows.zh: 性拘小忌，不許繕壁修牆，正瓦動屋。

before.literal: Given to petty taboos, he forbade plastering walls, repairing fences, or straightening roof-tiles.
before.idiomatic: He banned builders from touching plaster or tiles—superstition.

after.literal: Bound by petty taboos, he would not allow walls to be mended, roof tiles straightened, or the house disturbed.
after.idiomatic: Preoccupied with petty taboos, he would not allow walls repaired, roof tiles straightened, or the building disturbed.

rows.note: Restore 動屋; avoid introducing builders as agents.

rows.zh: 而于宮中為市，使人屠酤，手揣斤兩，輕重不差。

before.literal: Yet inside the palace he opened a market, had people butcher and sell ale, and weighed purchases in his own hands to the exact ounce.
before.idiomatic: Yet he ran a palace bazaar—himself butchering, selling ale, and weighing coin.

after.literal: Yet he set up a market in the palace, had people butcher and sell liquor, and estimated weights with his own hand without error.
after.idiomatic: Yet he set up a market in the palace, made others butcher and sell liquor, and could estimate an object’s weight by hand without error.

rows.note: 使人 assigns the butchering and selling to others; 揣斤兩 is estimating weight, not weighing coins or stating exact ounces.

rows.zh: 其母本屠家女也，故太子好之。

before.literal: His mother had been a butcher's daughter; therefore the crown prince delighted in it.
before.idiomatic: His mother's trade drew him to the stall.

after.literal: His mother had been a butcher's daughter; therefore the crown prince delighted in it.
after.idiomatic: His mother was originally a butcher’s daughter, which was why the crown prince enjoyed this.

rows.note: The source describes the mother’s family, not her own trade.

rows.zh: 東宮舊制，月請錢五十萬，備於眾用，太子恆探取二月，以供嬖寵。

before.literal: Eastern Palace precedent allotted five hundred thousand cash monthly for general expenses; the crown prince habitually drew two months ahead to supply favorites.
before.idiomatic: He drew double stipends to bankroll favorites.

after.literal: Eastern Palace precedent allotted five hundred thousand cash monthly for general expenses; the crown prince habitually drew two months ahead to supply favorites.
after.idiomatic: Under the Eastern Palace’s established rules, five hundred thousand cash were requested each month for common expenses, but the crown prince regularly drew two months’ funds in advance to support his favorites.

rows.note: Restore monthly amount and advance drawing, rather than an unexplained double stipend.

rows.zh: 洗馬江統陳五事以諫之，太子不納，語在《統傳》中。

before.literal: Groom of the Household Jiang Tong presented five admonitions; the crown prince rejected them—the account appears in Jiang Tong's biography.
before.idiomatic: Jiang Tong's five memorials went unheard—see his chapter.

after.literal: Jiang Tong, an Eastern Palace xima officer, submitted five points of remonstrance, but the crown prince did not accept them. The account is in Jiang Tong’s biography.
after.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace officer Jiang Tong urged him to reform on five points, but the crown prince rejected the advice; the account appears in Jiang Tong’s biography.

rows.note: 洗馬 is an institutional office; “groom” suggests a horse-handling function. The five points are not necessarily five separate memorials.

rows.zh: 舍人杜錫以太子非賈后所生，而後性凶暴，深以為憂，每盡忠規勸太子修德進善，遠於讒謗。

before.literal: Gentleman-of-the-Household Du Xi, because the crown prince was not Empress Jia's son and the empress was savage by nature, deeply worried; he repeatedly urged the crown prince to cultivate virtue and do good, standing far from slander.
before.idiomatic: Du Xi warned Yu to cultivate virtue—Jia was not his mother.

after.literal: Gentleman-of-the-Household Du Xi, because the crown prince was not Empress Jia's son and the empress was savage by nature, deeply worried; he repeatedly urged the crown prince to cultivate virtue and do good, standing far from slander.
after.idiomatic: Du Xi, a household officer, was deeply worried because the crown prince was not Empress Jia’s son and she was fierce and violent. He repeatedly urged the prince to cultivate virtue, do good, and keep clear of slander.

rows.note: Restore the empress’s character, Du’s concern, repeated counsel, and warning about slander.

rows.zh: 太子怒，使人以針著錫常所坐氈中而剌之。

before.literal: The crown prince grew angry and had someone sew needles into Du Xi's usual felt mat to stab him.
before.idiomatic: Yu pinned needles into Du Xi's seat cushion.

after.literal: The crown prince became angry and had someone place needles in the felt mat on which Du Xi usually sat, so that they pricked him.
after.idiomatic: Angered, the crown prince had needles placed in Du Xi’s usual felt seat to prick him.

rows.note: 使人 means he had another person do it; the source does not say sew.

rows.zh: 太子性剛，知賈謐恃後之貴，不能假借之。

before.literal: The crown prince's temper was stiff; knowing Jia Mi relied on the empress's power, he would not indulge him.
before.idiomatic: Yu refused to flatter Jia Mi.

after.literal: The crown prince's temper was stiff; knowing Jia Mi relied on the empress's power, he would not indulge him.
after.idiomatic: The crown prince was strong-willed. Knowing that Jia Mi relied on the empress’s power, he would not defer to him.

rows.note: Restore his character and the reason for his treatment of Jia Mi.

rows.zh: 謐至東宮，或舍之而於後庭遊戲。

before.literal: When Mi came to the Eastern Palace he sometimes left him waiting while he played in the inner courts.
before.idiomatic: He left Jia Mi cooling heels while he played inside.

after.literal: When Mi came to the Eastern Palace he sometimes left him waiting while he played in the inner courts.
after.idiomatic: When Jia Mi came to the Eastern Palace, the crown prince would sometimes leave him there and go to play in the rear court.

rows.note: Retain sometimes and the rear court.

rows.zh: 宜深自謙屈，以防其變，廣延賢士，用自輔翼。」

before.literal: You should humble yourself deeply to guard against change and broadly recruit worthy men to aid your wings.'
before.idiomatic: You should humble yourself deeply to guard against change and broadly recruit worthy men to aid your wings."

after.literal: You should humble yourself thoroughly to guard against such a change, and widely invite worthy men to assist you.
after.idiomatic: You should be genuinely modest and accommodating to guard against such trouble, and bring in worthy men to support you.

rows.note: 輔翼 is assistance, not literal wings.

rows.zh: 初，賈后母郭槐欲以韓壽女為太子妃，太子亦欲婚韓氏以自固。

before.literal: Earlier Empress Jia's mother Guo Huai had wished to take Han Shou's daughter as crown princess; the crown prince also wished to marry the Hans to strengthen himself.
before.idiomatic: Guo Huai once pushed a Han match—Yu wanted it too.

after.literal: Earlier Empress Jia's mother Guo Huai had wished to take Han Shou's daughter as crown princess; the crown prince also wished to marry the Hans to strengthen himself.
after.idiomatic: Earlier, Empress Jia’s mother Guo Huai wanted Han Shou’s daughter to become the crown princess, and the crown prince also wished to marry into the Han family to secure his position.

rows.note: Restore the people, proposed marriage, and the prince’s reason.

rows.zh: 而壽妻賈午及後皆不聽，而為太子聘王衍小女惠風。

before.literal: But Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused and instead betrothed the crown prince to Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng.
before.idiomatic: Jia Wu and the empress forced Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng instead.

after.literal: But Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused and instead betrothed the crown prince to Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng.
after.idiomatic: But Han Shou’s wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused, and instead arranged the crown prince’s betrothal to Wang Yan’s younger daughter, Huifeng.

rows.note: Preserve the betrothal and both named decision-makers; the source does not explicitly say she forced him.

rows.zh: 太子聞衍長女美，而賈后為謐聘之，心不能平，頗以為言。

before.literal: The crown prince heard Wang's elder daughter was beautiful while the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; his heart could not rest easy and he spoke of it often.
before.idiomatic: Yu resented losing Wang's elder beauty to Jia Mi.

after.literal: The crown prince heard Wang's elder daughter was beautiful while the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; his heart could not rest easy and he spoke of it often.
after.idiomatic: The crown prince heard that Wang Yan’s elder daughter was beautiful, but the empress had betrothed her to Jia Mi. Unable to put the matter aside, he spoke of it repeatedly.

rows.note: Restore that he heard of her beauty and voiced his displeasure.

rows.zh: 謐嘗與太子圍棋，爭道，成都王穎見而訶謐，謐意愈不平，因此譖太子于後曰：「太子廣買田業，多畜私財以結小人者，為賈氏故也。

before.literal: Once Mi played go with the crown prince and they quarreled over the move; Prince Chengdu of Ying saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and therefore slandered the crown prince to the empress: 'The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.
before.idiomatic: Once while playing go with the crown prince Mi quarreled over a move; Prince Chengdu of Ying saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and slandered the crown prince to the empress: "The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.

after.literal: Once Jia Mi played go with the crown prince, and they disputed a move. Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw this and rebuked Mi. Mi grew still more resentful and slandered the crown prince to the empress: “The crown prince is buying extensive lands and accumulating private wealth to win over petty men because of the Jia family.
after.idiomatic: Once Jia Mi quarreled with the crown prince over a move in a game of go. Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw it and scolded Mi, who grew more resentful and accused the prince before the empress: “He is buying up land and amassing wealth to win over petty men because of the Jia family.

rows.note: 成都王穎 is Ying, Prince of Chengdu, not Prince Chengdu of Ying; speech continues.

rows.zh: 密聞其言云：'皇后萬歲後，吾當魚肉之。

before.literal: And I secretly hear him say: After the empress dies I will butcher her like fish on the block.
before.idiomatic: Mi quoted Yu vowing to slaughter the Jias after Jia died.

after.literal: I secretly heard him say: ‘After the empress is gone, I will treat them as fish and meat.’
after.idiomatic: I secretly heard him say, ‘When the empress is gone, I will make fish and meat of them.’

rows.note: 魚肉 is a violent idiom; preceding Jia clan supplies likely plural referent, but no explicit promise to kill the empress herself. Speech continues.

rows.zh: '非但如是也，若宮車晏駕，彼居大位，依楊氏故事，誅臣等而廢後於金墉，如反手耳。

before.literal: Not only that—if the imperial carriage halts and he reaches the great seat, following Lady Yang's precedent he will execute us ministers and lock you away at Jinyong like turning his hand.
before.idiomatic: He warned Yu would purge Jia kin like the Yang coup.

after.literal: And that is not all. If the imperial carriage is delayed and he occupies the great throne, he could follow the precedent of the Yang family, execute us, and depose the empress at Jinyong as easily as turning over his hand.
after.idiomatic: And that is not all. If the emperor dies and the prince takes the throne, he could follow the precedent of the Yang family, execute us, and depose the empress at Jinyong as easily as turning his hand.

rows.note: 晏駕 euphemistically refers to the ruler’s death; retain the empress and Jinyong, and avoid asserting it was necessarily an actual Yang coup.

rows.zh: 後納其言，又宣揚太子之短，布諸遠近。

before.literal: The empress accepted his words and further broadcast the crown prince's faults throughout near and far.
before.idiomatic: Jia adopted the plot and smeared Yu empire-wide.

after.literal: The empress accepted his words and further broadcast the crown prince's faults throughout near and far.
after.idiomatic: The empress accepted his words and publicized the crown prince’s faults far and wide.

rows.note: The source says she publicized his faults, not necessarily that she invented them.

rows.zh: 于時朝野咸知賈后有害太子意。

before.literal: Then court and countryside knew the empress meant to harm the crown prince.
before.idiomatic: Everyone saw Jia meant to kill the heir.

after.literal: Then court and countryside knew the empress meant to harm the crown prince.
after.idiomatic: People at court and throughout the country all knew that Empress Jia intended to harm the crown prince.

rows.note: 有害 does not explicitly specify killing.

rows.zh: 中護軍趙俊請太子廢後，太子不聽。

before.literal: Central Guard Zhao Jun asked the crown prince to depose the empress first; the crown prince refused.
before.idiomatic: Zhao Jun urged preemptive deposition—Yu declined.

after.literal: Zhao Jun, the Central Protector of the Army, asked the crown prince to depose the empress, but the prince did not listen.
after.idiomatic: Zhao Jun, the Central Protector of the Army, urged the crown prince to depose the empress, but the prince refused to listen.

rows.note: Retain the office 中護軍 and avoid inserting “first” as an explicit word; review the standard English office title for consistency.

rows.zh: 九年六月，有桑生於宮西廂，日長尺餘，數日而枯。

before.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year a mulberry sprouted west of the palace, growing over a chi daily for days before withering.
before.idiomatic: Year nine saw an omen mulberry sprout west of the halls.

after.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year, a mulberry grew in the palace’s western wing. It grew more than a chi a day and withered after several days.
after.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the ninth year, a mulberry sprang up in the palace’s western wing. It grew more than a chi a day and withered after several days.

rows.note: Retain rate and withering; 宮西廂 identifies the palace western wing, not necessarily west of the palace.

rows.zh: 既至，後不見，置於別室，遣婢陳舞賜以酒棗，逼飲醉之。

before.literal: When he arrived she did not receive him but lodged him in a side chamber, sent maid Chen Wu with ale and jujubes, and forced him drunk.
before.idiomatic: She hid him, fed him wine and dates through Chen Wu until he was drunk.

after.literal: When he arrived she did not receive him but lodged him in a side chamber, sent maid Chen Wu with ale and jujubes, and forced him drunk.
after.idiomatic: When he arrived, the empress did not receive him. She put him in a separate room, sent the maid Chen Wu to give him wine and dates, and forced him to drink until he was drunk.

rows.note: Restore separate room and forced drinking; no need to infer concealment.

rows.zh: 使黃門侍郎潘岳作書草，若禱神之文，有如太子素意，因醉而書之，令小婢承福以紙筆及書草使太子書之。

before.literal: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the crown prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, giving small maid Chengfu paper, brush, and draft.
before.idiomatic: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the Crown Prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.

after.literal: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a text like a prayer to the spirits, as though it expressed the crown prince’s own intentions. Taking advantage of his drunkenness, she had the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and the draft and make him copy it.
after.idiomatic: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the Crown Prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.

rows.note: Pair literal with existing independently reviewed idiomatic: Chengfu brings the materials rather than simply receiving them.

rows.zh: 文曰：「陛下宜自了；

before.literal: The text read: 'Your Majesty should settle matters himself.
before.idiomatic: Forgery opened: 'Father must finish this himself.

after.literal: The text read: 'Your Majesty should settle matters himself.
after.idiomatic: The text said: “Your Majesty should bring matters to an end yourself;

rows.note: Retain the explicitly written form of address and ambiguous 自了; avoid claiming the forged text specifies father or murder.

rows.zh: 不自了，吾當入了之。

before.literal: If you do not settle them I will finish them for you.
before.idiomatic: Or I will finish you.

after.literal: If you do not settle them I will finish them for you.
after.idiomatic: if you do not bring them to an end yourself, I will enter and do so.

rows.note: Preserve the ambiguity and 入; “finish you” asserts an interpretation rather than the words.

rows.zh: 中宮又宜速自了；

before.literal: The inner palace should likewise settle matters quickly.
before.idiomatic: The empress must settle too.

after.literal: The inner palace should likewise settle matters quickly.
after.idiomatic: The empress, too, should quickly bring matters to an end herself;

rows.note: Retain the adverb quickly and parallel construction.

rows.zh: 不了，吾當手了之。

before.literal: If she does not settle them I will finish her with my own hand.
before.idiomatic: Or I will kill her myself.

after.literal: If she does not settle them I will finish her with my own hand.
after.idiomatic: if she does not, I will do so with my own hand.

rows.note: Keep ambiguity parallel with the source; the threat may imply killing but should not be asserted as the only literal reading.

rows.zh: 並謝妃共要克期而兩發，勿疑猶豫，致後患。

before.literal: Together with Consort Xie we agreed a joint date for simultaneous rising—do not hesitate and breed later trouble.
before.idiomatic: Consort Xie and I strike together—no delay.

after.literal: Together with Consort Xie we agreed a joint date for simultaneous rising—do not hesitate and breed later trouble.
after.idiomatic: Consort Xie and I have agreed on a date to act together. Do not hesitate and bring trouble upon us later.

rows.note: Restore agreed date, joint action, and future danger.

rows.zh: 茹毛飲血於三辰之下，皇天許當掃除患害，立道文為王，蔣為內主。

before.literal: We shall eat raw flesh and drink blood beneath the three luminaries; High Heaven grants us leave to sweep away the scourge, enthrone Daowen as king, and install Jiang as inner mistress.
before.idiomatic: Heaven blesses our coup—crown Daowen, empower Lady Jiang.

after.literal: Eating raw flesh and drinking blood beneath the three luminaries, may Heaven permit the removal of the dangers, the establishment of Daowen as king, and Jiang as mistress of the inner palace.
after.idiomatic: Eating raw flesh and drinking blood beneath the sun, moon, and stars, we call on Heaven to grant that we sweep away the danger, make Daowen king, and install Jiang as mistress of the inner palace.

rows.note: Restore oath imagery and named objects; 皇天許當 is not a verified prediction that Heaven approved a coup. Review the prayer’s syntax independently.

rows.zh: 願成，當三牲祠北君，大赦天下。

before.literal: When wish is fulfilled we shall sacrifice three victims to the Northern Lord and proclaim an empire-wide amnesty.
before.idiomatic: Then sacrifice to the Northern Lord and amnesty all.

after.literal: When wish is fulfilled we shall sacrifice three victims to the Northern Lord and proclaim an empire-wide amnesty.
after.idiomatic: If our wish is fulfilled, we shall sacrifice three animals to the Northern Lord and grant an amnesty throughout the realm.

rows.note: Restore condition and 三牲.

rows.zh: 太子醉迷不覺，遂依而寫之，其字半不成。

before.literal: The crown prince was too drunk and confused to notice; he copied accordingly; half the characters failed to form.
before.idiomatic: Blind drunk, he traced childish strokes.

after.literal: The crown prince was too drunk and confused to notice; he copied accordingly; half the characters failed to form.
after.idiomatic: The crown prince was so drunk and confused that he did not realize what he was doing, and copied the text; half the characters were not properly formed.

rows.note: Restore copying and incomplete characters; do not add childish strokes.

rows.zh: 既而補成之，后以呈帝。

before.literal: They afterward filled them in; the empress presented it to the emperor.
before.idiomatic: Helpers patched characters before Jia showed Hui.

after.literal: They afterward filled them in; the empress presented it to the emperor.
after.idiomatic: Afterward the characters were completed, and the empress showed the text to the emperor.

rows.note: The actor completing characters is unspecified; avoid inventing helpers.

rows.zh: 遍示諸公王，莫有言者，惟張華、裴頠證明太子。

before.literal: No one among lords and dukes spoke except Zhang Hua and Pei Wei who verified the crown prince's innocence.
before.idiomatic: Silence fell until Zhang Hua and Pei Wei defended Yu.

after.literal: It was shown to all the dukes and princes, and none spoke except Zhang Hua and Pei Wei, who testified for the crown prince.
after.idiomatic: The text was shown to all the dukes and princes. None spoke except Zhang Hua and Pei Wei, who testified in the crown prince’s defense.

rows.note: Restore distribution to the assembled dukes and princes.

rows.zh: 議至日西不決。

before.literal: Deliberation lasted until sunset unresolved.
before.idiomatic: Debate stalled till dusk.

after.literal: The deliberations continued until the sun was in the west, without a decision.
after.idiomatic: The debate remained unresolved into the late afternoon.

rows.note: 日西 means the sun had moved west; sunset is more specific than the text.

rows.zh: 後懼事變，乃表免太子為庶人，詔許之。

before.literal: The empress feared events might shift and therefore memorialized to degrade the crown prince to commoner status; an edict approved.
before.idiomatic: Jia feared delay—demoted Yu to commoner instead.

after.literal: The empress feared events might shift and therefore memorialized to degrade the crown prince to commoner status; an edict approved.
after.idiomatic: Afraid that matters might change, the empress petitioned to demote the crown prince to commoner status instead, and an edict granted her request.

rows.note: Retain her petition and imperial approval.

rows.zh: 於是使尚書和郁持節，解結為副，及大將軍梁王肜、鎮東將軍淮南王允、前將軍東武公澹、趙王倫、太保何劭詣東宮，廢太子為庶人。

before.literal: Thereupon Minister Director He Yu was dispatched with insignia, Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Prince Liang of Liang, Eastern Garrison Prince Huainan of Yun, Forward General Eastern Martial Duke Dan, Prince Zhao of Lun, and Grand Tutor He Shao to the Eastern Palace to depose the crown prince as commoner.
before.idiomatic: Thereupon Minister Director He Yu was dispatched with insignia, with Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Sima Tong, Prince of Liang; Eastern Garrison General Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan; Forward General Sima Dan, Eastern Martial Duke; Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao; and Grand Tutor He Shao. They went to the Eastern Palace to depose the Crown Prince as a commoner.

after.literal: Thereupon He Yu of the Secretariat was sent bearing credentials, with Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Rong, Prince of Liang; Yun, Prince of Huainan and General Who Guards the East; Dan, Duke of Dongwu and Forward General; Lun, Prince of Zhao; and Grand Guardian He Shao. They went to the Eastern Palace and demoted the crown prince to a commoner.
after.idiomatic: He Yu of the Secretariat was then sent with credentials, with Xie Jie as his deputy. Accompanying them were General-in-Chief Sima Rong, Prince of Liang; Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan and General Who Guards the East; Sima Dan, Duke of Dongwu and Forward General; Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao; and Grand Guardian He Shao. They went to the Eastern Palace to depose the crown prince and reduce him to commoner status.

rows.note: Correct 王肜 (Rong), 王允 (Yun), 公澹 (Dan), 王倫 (Lun); 太保 should be rendered consistently as Grand Guardian. The existing independently reviewed idiomatic expands them to Sima names but calls 肜 Sima Tong. A new independent review must reconcile that receipt rather than silently overriding it.

rows.zh: 是日太子游玄圃，聞有使者至，改服出崇賢門，再拜受詔，步出承華門，乘粗犢車。

before.literal: That day the crown prince roamed the Mystic Garden; hearing envoys arrived he changed clothes, exited Chongxian Gate, twice bowed receiving the edict, walked out Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart.
before.idiomatic: Yu took the edict from the garden and rode an ox-cart out.

after.literal: That day the crown prince roamed the Mystic Garden; hearing envoys arrived he changed clothes, exited Chongxian Gate, twice bowed receiving the edict, walked out Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart.
after.idiomatic: That day the crown prince was in the Xuanpu garden. On hearing that envoys had arrived, he changed clothes, came out through Chongxian Gate, bowed twice to receive the edict, walked out through Chenghua Gate, and rode in a plain ox cart.

rows.note: Restore change of clothing, gates, double bow and sequence.

rows.zh: 澹以兵仗送太子妃王氏、三皇孫于金墉城，考竟謝淑妃及太子保林蔣俊。

before.literal: Dan escorted Crown Princess Wang and three imperial grandsons to Jinyong with armed guards, interrogated Consort-in-chief Xie and heir guardian Jiang Jun to death.
before.idiomatic: Dan marched Wang consort and grandsons to Jinyong—executed Xie and Jiang Jun.

after.literal: Dan sent the crown princess, Lady Wang, and the three imperial grandsons to Jinyong under armed escort. Consort Xie and the crown prince’s baolin, Jiang Jun, were interrogated to death.
after.idiomatic: Dan sent the crown princess, Lady Wang, and the three imperial grandsons to Jinyong under armed guard; Consort Xie and the prince’s baolin Jiang Jun were interrogated to death.

rows.note: 考竟 means investigation to death in context, not mere execution; 保林 is a palace consort rank, not guardian. Review “her” against uncertainty about maternity; no biological relationship to Wang is asserted by the source.

holds.note: 藍子 can mean indigo seeds or be a textual variant of 籃子 (baskets); 面 may mean flour or noodles. Compare the actual base edition and Jinshu 056 Jiang Tong before proposing replacements.
Grammatical subject of 而有不順之色 requires review; avoid asserting Jia Mi rather than the crown prince displayed disrespect without contextual evidence.
要疏如律令 is a prayer/talisman formula; review exact reading and translation from an authoritative ritual source before changing either field.
乙太子書 may reflect corrupted 以; retain source issue for independently verified textual restoration and clarify action, not silent emendation.
Existing approved idiomatic says Sima Tong for 肜 (Sima Rong) and Grand Tutor for 太保; rectify both fields without overriding the existing decision receipt silently.
